thread:
sara: Paging—seeing sustained p99 latency spikes for single-tenant s-123 (Streamly) starting ~10:02 UTC. Symptoms: streaming stalls, stalled chunks, increased end-to-end tail latency. Noticed during a large burst of concurrent sessions. Graph: https://grafana.redwood.prod/d/streamly/slo?orgId=1 :rotating_light:

incident_bot: ALERT: service=runtime-inference, tenant=s-123, metric=p99_latency, window=5m, value=6.2s (SLO=1.5s) — severity=page — triggered at 2026-03-14T10:02:12Z

sara: @raj @mike can you pick this up? Looks customer-impacting, single-tenant high concurrency.

raj: ack. oncall for eng-runtime here. Pulling logs + tailing streaming proxy logs now. Any quick mitigation ideas?

mike: pulling node metrics. Early signal: memory climb on a few replicas serving s-123, and a large fraction of requests are long-context prompts (many code fences + long system messages) causing KV cache pressure and repeated attention recompute. Also seeing many streaming connections stuck waiting for heartbeats.

alice: CS: Streamly ran a heavy internal load test (they said ~400–500 concurrent streams) to validate their rollout. They flagged stalliness ~10:01 UTC.

raj: copying runbook section "single-tenant tail latency" now. Immediate mitigations I can do: 1) route tenant to smaller model variant; 2) apply per-tenant concurrency throttle; 3) enable conservative batching/disable streaming for that tenant. Which do we pick first?

sara: prioritize least customer-visible first: 1) apply concurrency cap 50rps for s-123, 2) pin to model v-small-1 as fallback for new requests (preserve ongoing streams), 3) if needed revert prefix caching behavior. Also ask CS to pause their test.

raj: executing throttle and route. Commands:
```bash
# throttle (temporary):
redwoodctl tenants update s-123 --concurrency=50
# pin new requests to fallback model:
redwoodctl route update --tenant s-123 --model=small-v1 --mode=new
```

oncall_bot: ACTION LOGGED: @raj applied tenant concurrency cap and model pin. See /incidents/1769812345/actions

mike: after the cap and pin, p95 dropped from ~900ms to ~220ms in the last 90s for new sessions. However ongoing streaming sessions still show stalls — probably due to long prompt hotpath and KV cache pressure. I'm going to recycle the three worst nodes (g4-12x.x). Will drain gracefully.

raj: nodes drained and restarted. Clearing KV cache on affected hosts.

mike: restarted replicas and cleared caches. Streaming stalls reduced for many sessions but we still see occasional chunk delays for prompts >4k tokens. Investigating whether our streaming chunker is waiting on partial attention recompute for huge contexts.

sara: enable response-heartbeat feature for tenant to keep client connections alive while we triage. Also lower max_new_tokens for the tenant to limit single-response compute.

raj: applied heartbeat and set max_new_tokens=512 for s-123.

incident_bot: NOTE: config change detected for tenant s-123: heartbeat=on, max_new_tokens=512 by raj.

alice: I told Streamly support to pause the remaining batch and collect problematic prompt samples (anonymized). They agreed to stop additional load for now.

mike: got a sample prompt that reproduces the hotpath: many nested triple-backtick blocks and long inline eval code. It's causing attention to blow past our typical sequence-length distribution and triggers slower kernels. We'll add a guard to detect repeated code fence patterns and short-circuit with a summary or token limit.

sara: impact summary for ops: one tenant (s-123) saw p99 > 5s for ~14 minutes; p95 briefly exceeded SLO; root cause likely combination of unusual prompt shape + sustained very high concurrency exhausting KV/prefix caching heuristics for that tenant. Mitigation: throttle, pin fallback model, restart nodes, enable heartbeat + token caps.

raj: creating incident page with timeline and action items. Marking priority=P2 (customer impact, single tenant).

mike: short-term engineering items: (a) add guardrail on prompt length/patterns to fast-fail or summarize before attention blowups, (b) improve streaming chunk timeouts and emit telemetry when chunk build time > 300ms, (c) add tenant-level retry/fallback to non-streaming mode after N stalled chunks.

sara: ops/postmortem items for follow-up: update runbook with clear step to apply per-tenant heartbeat + token caps, add an automated detector for "code-fence heavy" prompts, and provide CS with best-practice guidance for load tests (throttle/concurrency targets).

raj: handing off to @lina for next oncall. Notes in incident page + pinned grafana link. Lina — I left the tenant pinned to small-v1 with concurrency=50 and heartbeat enabled. Watch for regression and coordinate with eng-runtime if you need to flip back.

lina: ack — I'll monitor for the next 2 hours and follow up with a postmortem draft. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
